checks.description: lists all four quarters in order

query: Write a Python module solution.py exposing a function `merge_intervals(intervals)` that merges overlapping closed intervals and returns them sorted by start. Verify it yourself before finishing.

checks.code:
from solution import merge_intervals
assert merge_intervals([[1,3],[2,6],[8,10]]) == [[1,6],[8,10]]
assert merge_intervals([]) == []
assert merge_intervals([[1,4],[4,5]]) == [[1,5]]

query: Create a directory named logs/ holding three files a.log, b.log and c.log. Each must have at least 8 lines, and exactly 7 lines across all three must contain the word ERROR. Then count those ERROR lines with shell commands and write just that number into error_count.txt.

checks.code: test -f logs/a.log && test -f logs/b.log && test -f logs/c.log
test "$(cat logs/a.log logs/b.log logs/c.log | grep -c ERROR)" = 7
test "$(tr -d '[:space:]' < error_count.txt)" = "$(cat logs/a.log logs/b.log logs/c.log | grep -c ERROR)"
checks.description: the recorded count matches a fresh recount

query: Create a CSV file data.csv with a header line `name,score` and exactly 5 data rows of your choosing. Then compute the mean score and write it, rounded to 2 decimal places, into mean.txt as the only content.

checks.code:
import csv
with open('data.csv') as f:
    rows = list(csv.DictReader(f))
assert len(rows) == 5, len(rows)
mean = sum(float(r['score']) for r in rows) / len(rows)
got = float(open('mean.txt').read().strip())
assert abs(got - round(mean, 2)) < 0.01, (got, mean)
checks.description: mean.txt matches the mean recomputed from data.csv
